sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.3676 of 2024
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for respondent No.1, Sri Ravikanthi Madhubabu, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent Nos.2 to 4 and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent No.5,
and perused the record.

2. The petitioner is aggrieved by the action of the respondents in determining the compensation amount payable in a sum of Rs.1,68,995/- in respect of the land to an extent of Ac.0.350 cents in Sy.No.160A/3/3 situated at Bingidoddi Village, Ieeja Mandal, Jogulambna Gadwal District,
acquired for construction/development of Six Lane Access Controlled Greenfield Highway and in not releasing the said amount to him, as being illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, 'the Act').

3. Petitioner contends that though the respondents-authorities have acquired his land to an extent of Ac.0.350 cents and having determined the compensation amount payable in a sum of Rs.1,68,995/-, however, did not make the aforesaid payment to him, in spite of his name was shown in the preliminary notification issued under Section 3A as well as declaration issued under Section 3D of the Act and thus, being entitled to receive the said compensation amount.
4.

Per contra, learned Government Pleader appearing on behalf of respondent No.5 submits that an award was passed by the said respondent on 27.12.2021, in respect of various extents of land; that insofar as the land of the petitioner in Sy.No.160 is concerned, the authorities have noted that as per 1971 Pahani and old ROR, the said land was shown as Ceiling Patta Land having a total extent of Acs.8.13 guntas; that the ceiling surplus land thereafter was assigned to 1. Sri Devadanam S/o Doddeppa and 2. Sri Chinna Thirumanna s/o Jammanna to an extent of Acs.4.00 guntas and Acs.4.13 guntas respectively

; that after the demise of Sri Chinna Thimmanna, the assigned land was divided between his two sons namely 1. Sri Hr. Anandam and 2. Sri Charles to an extent of Acs.2.06 guntas and Acs.2.07 guntas respectively by assigning sub- division Nos.160/A and 160/A/2 and were issued with pattadar pass book with Khatha Nos.449 & 450; that out of the said total extent,
land belonging to the said assignee, an extent of Ac.1.750 cents was coming under proposed acquisition; that on the respondents-authorities issuing notice proposing to acquire the above said extent of land, including the land being claimed by the petitioner, the petitioner and four others Kurva Chinna Hanmanthu vs The Union Of India on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45783417/
1 (including the two sons of assignee of ceiling surplus land) filed petition seeking for payment of compensation towards land proposed to be acquired in an amount of Rs.45,00,000/- per acre, but did not produce any documentary evidence to support their claim.

sentences.text:
5. Learned Government Pleader further submits that since, the petitioner did not produce any documentary evidence supporting his claim of compensation in a sum of Rs.45,00,000/- per acre,
the respondents- authorities have passed the award determining the market value of the land to be in a sum of Rs.52,500/- per acre.
6.

Learned Government Pleader would further submit that since, there is a dispute with regard to the land admeasuring Ac.1.750 cents, the authorities have decided that the compensation amount to the extent of Ac.1.750 cents, which includes the land to an extent of Ac.0.350 cents being claimed by the petitioner to be deposited before the Court of Principal Senior Civil Judge, Gadwal, by making a reference under Section 3H(4) of the Act.

7. Learned Government Pleader further submits that since, the authorities have noted that there is a dispute in respect of the aforesaid land, vide O.S.No.115 of 2012 pending on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Gadwal, the authorities have deposited the amount of compensation, vide proceedings No.G/1013/2018 dt.17.01.2023, into the said Court.

8. Learned Government Pleader further submits that since, the authorities have deposited the compensation amount determined before the Competent Court in terms of Section 3H(4) of the Act,
noting the existence of a land dispute, the petitioner has to approach the concerned Court to establish his title over the land in order to claim the aforesaid compensation amount and thus, the present Writ Petition as filed seeking payment of the compensation is not maintainable.
9.
I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.

10. The respondents-authorities having passed an award on 27.12.2021, in respect of various extents of land admeasuring Ac.1.750 cents in Sy.No.160, which, inter alia, includes the land being claimed by the petitioner admeasuring Ac.0.350 cents, and the respondents- authorities having noted that there exists a land dispute pending consideration before the Civil Court in O.S.No.115 of 2012; and having deposited the compensation amount determined in respect of the said land in a sum of Rs.1,68,995/- by making a reference under Section 3H(4) of the Act, this Court is of the view that the petitioner instead of approaching this Court by way of present Writ Petition seeking a direction for payment of the aforesaid compensation amount, is required to approach the concerned Court to which a reference has been made by the respondents-authorities, and establish his right and interest over the subject land in order to claim the aforesaid compensation deposited by the respondents-authorities.
Thus, the petitioner is not entitled for being granted with any relief in the present Writ Petition.

11. In view of the above, this Court is of the view that the petitioner should be directed to approach the concerned Court to which reference has been made by the respondents-authorities, under Section 3H(4) of the Act and claim the compensation amount from the concerned Court by Kurva Chinna Hanmanthu vs The Union Of India on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45783417/
2 establishing his title to the subject land acquired.

sentences.text: 12. Subject to above observation and direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
13. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
